rationale: MAA/RN/2025/04 (effective 10 October 2025) directly supports the claim text without overstatement. Paragraph 6 states that for Certified Air Systems, applicants should raise a Military Certification Review Item (MCRI) for MAA agreement. Paragraph 7 explicitly recommends that early applications of ML techniques use training methods such as supervised learning to generate models that remain fixed for system integration and use within a defined operational design domain (ODD). The claim properly characterizes these elements as applicant-specific guidance and recommendations rather than mandatory universal certification rules, and the scoped boundary explicitly excludes civil airworthiness approval or product safety cases.
evidence_locators: MAA/RN/2025/04 Version 5.0, p. 1, paras 2–3 (Scope and Implementation)
MAA/RN/2025/04 Version 5.0, p. 2, paras 6–7 (Certified Air Systems)
limitations: Underlying MMAC procedures and completed project-specific MCRIs remain proprietary/non-public to the UK Ministry of Defence and specific applicants.
MAA regulatory notices are informative guidance for the Defence Air Environment and cannot be transferred to civil airworthiness certification (FAA/EASA).
